claims.content: The RLCS software monitors the status of all field devices and processes operator requests for changing field device status.

goal.raw_text: The RLCS software monitors the status of all field devices and processes operator requests for changing field device status.

claims.content: Operator

The RLCS software startup process must have completed successfully, which includes identifying the unit, verifying required cards, performing a control system integrity check, and initializing specified tables.
Each workstation and control unit (FCU or DCU) must be online and identified by the system along with its associated device sensors.
The Operator must be logged in to the RLCS network computer.
The Operator must possess the appropriate access level and be using an authorized workstation.
The Operator logs into the RLCS system to monitor facility and device status, or a field device sensor reports a status change.

trigger.raw_text: The Operator logs into the RLCS system to monitor facility and device status, or a field device sensor reports a status change.

claims.content: The RLCS software displays the facility geographic area, traffic flow direction, customer eligibility, and device sensor status using dynamic icons on the GUI.
The system continually updates the status information every 2 seconds, even when no user is logged on.
If a device enters an alarm state, the GUI issues an audible alarm and changes the device icon color to distinguish it from the normal status.
The Monitor Devices process receives Device Sensor Status data from field devices and passes it to the Set Alarms and Collect Log Data processes.
The Operator can set the operational status of failed devices using a control option.
The Operator can view active overrides and identify which devices have no currently active 'rules protection' against erroneous opening/closing.
The Operator can turn off the audible alarm permanently or temporarily for a given period.
The Operator can configure alarm conditions on the screen.
If a device status has been overridden, it appears on the screen with a different color from the normal and alarm status colors.
During 'degraded' mode, the system monitors device sensors at a frequency rate stored in the database specific to that mode.

At any point in an opening or closing sequence, the sequence shall be halted if: (1) A device fails to report completion of the current sequence step within the response time window allotted for the step; (2) The status of a closure device, which was previously opened at the current entrance, changes to 'unknown' or 'closed', without an operator-initiated command; (3) The status of a closure device, which was previously closed at the current entrance, changes to 'unknown' or 'open', without an operator-initiated command.
At any point in an opening sequence, the sequence shall be halted if the status of a closure device for the opposite direction of travel changes to 'unknown' or 'open'.

To resume an opening or closing sequence after a halt has occurred, the operator shall be able to issue a command to resume if the offending device status can be corrected within a configurable time period as defined in the database and in non-volatile memory.
The current status of all entrance closure devices is maintained at each control unit and updated across all control units in the system.
Any change in device state is reported on the screen not later than 2 seconds from the time it occurs.
The system has monitored field controllers and connected devices on the RLCS network for control system integrity.
All users logged in to RLCS network computers and all commands issued in the field units have been reported by the system.
If a critical alarm condition was met during monitoring, the system has generated and presented the appropriate alarm to the operator.
